title: Negative assertions for lazily mounted providers must run after waitFor
answers: how to test custom view provider is omitted when disabled
jest test negative assertion async flush sessions page
body:
In ExperimentSingleChatSessionPage.test.tsx, the disabled-path and outer-definition tests are async and assert inside waitFor.
This is needed because the provider is reached through React.lazy and Suspense, so a synchronous not.toHaveBeenCalled can pass before the lazy tree flushes.
The test mocks ExperimentCustomViewProvider via jest.mock on the traces-v3 path and clears the mock in beforeEach.
Run the test with the Jest setup used for the MLflow JS app; the shouldEnableModelTraceExplorerCustomTraceView mock is set per test with mockReturnValue.
applies: Jest tests for pages that lazy-load optional providers gated by a feature flag.
says: The custom trace view still displays in chat sessions when the feature flag is disabled.
Hide the custom trace explorer view on experiment chat session pages when turned off.
Custom view component unexpectedly loads on chat session page despite being disabled in settings.
Ensure turning off the custom trace view feature completely removes it from chat sessions.
